commit_message: GATE-08: recovery — link failure detection, route invalidation, alternative gateway discovery, new route/circuit (no TCP migration)
scope_completed: Link degradation/down detection (handleLinkEvent with DOWN/DEGRADED status)
Gateway disappearance handling (handleGatewayDisappearance: all links DOWN + all routes through gateway invalidated)
Alternative gateway discovery (discoverAlternativeGateways: LINK_UP + capability match + exclude failed + sort by latency)
Recovery plan creation (createRecoveryPlan: DISCOVER_NEW_GATEWAY / WAIT_FOR_LINK_RECOVERY / NO_RECOVERY_POSSIBLE)
No claim of arbitrary TCP migration (TCP_MIGRATION_FORBIDDEN architecture guard + recommendation text)
Full recovery flow: Gateway A disappears → Gateway B discovered → new route → new circuit → new flow (test #10)
12 unit tests covering all recovery scenarios
protocol_adr_references: spec/00 §9 (Recovery: gateway disappears → route invalidated → gateway discovered → new route → new circuit → new flow)
spec/00 §22 (Routing: discovery ≠ path validation ≠ route ≠ circuit)
known_limitations: Real-process recovery integration test is deferred — the unit tests prove the recovery state machine with in-memory state. The integration test will exercise the mini-services (gateway process killed → alternative discovered → new route → new circuit → new flow succeeds).
The RecoveryManager is in-memory only. A production implementation would need to persist route/circuit health across restarts.

Link health detection (how DEGRADED is determined — latency thresholds, packet loss) is not yet implemented. The RecoveryManager accepts health events but does not generate them — that's the transport layer's responsibility.
